title: Comparing N-HITS and PatchTST against Chronos-2, TimesFM, Toto, and Granite TTM on real weekly stock calls, hash-committed before market open
author: MasterpieceLumpy619
selftext:
I built an app (TensorSwing) that runs 7 forecasting models against each other on a fixed universe of 119 stocks and ETFs. Two are neural nets I trained myself, N-HITS and PatchTST, both run with Monte Carlo passes for uncertainty. The other five are pretrained time-series foundation models: Chronos and Chronos-2 from Amazon, TimesFM from Google, Toto from Datadog, and Granite TTM from IBM (that one runs behind its own sidecar service).

Every Monday, each model calls 5-day direction and size for every name in the universe. Calls are cryptographically hashed and timestamped at publication so nothing can be edited or walked back later. Friday's closes settle each call, every model gets scored separately, and a public randomness beacon we don't control spot-checks a sample each Saturday. The full record stays in a public archive, win or lose.

The models disagree a lot. The app shows that disagreement instead of collapsing it into one consensus number.

Free tier gets the watchlist and this week's field. Premium is $39/mo and unlocks every model's individual call plus the full per-model track record.

This is informational research, not investment advice. No brokerage connection, no trades placed.
